geometry_edits.rationale: Split the dominant bulk into two linked wings to open a more legible ground void toward the access edge while preserving one primary anchored mass.
Orient the split along the frontage axis so the public threshold becomes visible in plan and section.
Create a measured gap that can operate as entry court/void rather than a mere surface notch.
Keep the mass readable as one continuous project through a connector, avoiding fragmentation.
Make the new split-wing dominant form the root so the revised public void and hierarchy govern the whole massing.

graph_edits.rationale: Change the dominant mass from a purely projecting cantilever into a lifted base with a clearer ground threshold and more legible public undercut.
Reduce the horizontal overhang and re-balance the lifted mass so the access edge can read as occupied public ground rather than a sealed bulk.
Add a compatible public void attached to the dominant mass to strengthen the frontage response and support neighborhood-active ground space.
Keep the void substantial enough to read as usable public space rather than decorative subtraction.
Align the public opening to the programmed access side so the court addresses the street threshold coherently.

rationale: The candidate reads as one coherent dominant mass with a stepped/cantilevered upper profile, and it is visible in all four views without obvious self-collision. The parcel containment appears respected, so it passes the deterministic hard gate. Programmatically, the mass can plausibly support neighborhood-living/commercial use as a compact street building, but the access-edge response is weak: the thick blue frontage is not answered by a clearly public void, notch, or entry seam, so the ground condition feels sealed and semantically muted. The silhouette is more coherent than arbitrary, and the section has some upper hierarchy, but the void/publicness score remains low because the court/terrace logic is not legible enough as usable public space. Overall this is a salvageable early massing with a strong anchor but insufficient public-threshold articulation.
